chunks: And from him, from a group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Ali ibn Abd al-'Aziz, from Murad ibn Kharajah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, when it is Friday and the sun is from the east as much as it is from the west, at the time of the 'Asr prayer, I pray six rak'at. When the day rises, I pray six. When the sun declines or moves away, I pray two rak'at, then I pray Dhuhr, then I pray six after it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific sequence of voluntary prayers performed by the Imam on Friday according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s family’s distinct devotional rhythm on Fridays, emphasizing the multiplication of voluntary prayers (Sunnah) at key solar transitions to sanctify the day. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Tawqifi* practices, where specific timings and quantities of *Nafl* prayers are derived from the Imams' personal precedents to complement the obligatory *Fard* prayers.
